study: warm-agent reuse — does one deploy survive repeated runs with telemetry intact?
why: The canonical 12-run deploys a fresh agent for every leg (every leg sets teardown:true), which
was adopted deliberately to dodge the warm-agent token-attribution loss. That design means the
12-run can never test whether the loss is fixed: it never reuses an agent. This spec does the
Leg #1 deploys and is the cold reference. Legs #2-#4 carry no deploy_body, so the driver leaves
the deployment alone and the same agent process serves run after run. Task selection is
deterministic, so all four legs run the SAME five gsm8k tasks and the token columns are directly
Two defects are read off one run of this spec:
span loss  — the structural test llm_count<=1 AND tool_count>=2 is impossible (a tool call
needs a preceding model turn), so any row matching it in #2-#4 but not #1 is the
warm-agent loss. Do NOT use tokens==0: the probe's own usage is model-dependent.
response caching — if litellm caching is live, #2 replays #1's completions instead of calling
the model. That shows up as a collapse in latency at unchanged pass rate, not as
a token anomaly, so compare total_latency_s across legs as well as tokens.
#4 repeats the reuse at max_parallel_sessions=4 because the two defects have different
concurrency signatures and a serial-only result would not generalise to legs #3-#12.

legs.title: 1 — gsm8k 5 tasks p=1 — fresh deploy, cold reference
legs.deploy: fresh deploy; this deployment is kept up and reused by #2-#4

legs.title: 2 — gsm8k 5 tasks p=1 — REUSE #1's agent (2nd run on one process)
legs.deploy: no deploy_body: the driver skips deploy and teardown entirely

legs.title: 3 — gsm8k 5 tasks p=1 — REUSE again (3rd run on one process)
legs.deploy: no deploy_body; a 3rd run distinguishes 'only the 2nd run breaks' from 'all reuse breaks'

legs.title: 4 — gsm8k 5 tasks p=4 — REUSE under concurrency
legs.deploy: no deploy_body; concurrency is where the cache-hit-callback thread path appears
